questions.text: Define and develop a Poker test for four-digit random numbers. A sequence of 10,000 random numbers, each of four digits has been generated. The analysis of the numbers reveals that in 5120 numbers all four digits are different, 4230 contain exactly one pair of like digits, 560 contain two pairs, 75 have three digits of a kind and 15 contain all like digits. Use Poker test to determine whether these numbers are independent. (Critical value of chisquare test for α=0.05 and N=4 is 9.49).

marking_scheme.point: Defines Poker test and states its purpose for assessing independence of digits.
States the null ($H_0$) and alternative ($H_1$) hypotheses correctly.
Correctly identifies all 5 poker hand categories and derives their theoretical probabilities (e.g., $P(\text{ABCD}) = \frac{10 \times 9 \times 8 \times 7}{10^4}$).
Calculates all 5 expected frequencies ($E_i = N \times P_i$).
Calculates the Chi-square statistic using the formula $\sum \frac{(O_i - E_i)^2}{E_i}$ and performs all individual calculations correctly.
States the degrees of freedom ($k-1$) and correctly compares the calculated $\chi^2$ with the given critical value.
Draws a correct conclusion based on the comparison, interpreting it in the context of random number independence.
